To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the $\nu_e + n \rightarrow p + e^- $ and $\bar\nu_e + p \rightarrow n + e^+ $ absorption rates in the outer layers of a neutron star (the neutrino-sphere) are significantly enhanced and suppressed, respectively, by nuclear mean-fields.

(1) the charged-current neutrino absorption cross-sections in the supernova are strongly enhanced due to the presence of the nuclear medium, (2) the enhancement is larger for the $\nu_e+n$ reaction than for the $\bar{\nue}+p$ reaction, and (3) the difference in the absorption rates for the two reactions is larger than previously thought.
the charged-current neutrino-nucleus reactions $\nu_e + N \to e^- + p$ and $\bar{\nue} + N \to p + e^+$ in supernovae have a large asymmetry between the rates of the two reactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neutrino-nucleon cross-sections in the supernova environment and the nucleosynthesis that results.
the neutrino absorption rates in the neutrino sphere of a supernova.
the study of the neutrino-spherical shell in supernovae.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neutrino absorption rates are larger in the outer regions and the neutrino emission rates larger in the inner regions of the supernova.
the neutrino absorption cross-sections are larger than the ones obtained in previous studies.
the $\nu_{\rm e}$ absorption rate is enhanced and the $\bar{\bar{\nu}_{\rm e}}$ absorption rate is suppressed by the nuclear mean-field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the $\bar{\nue}$ absorption rates are suppressed by a factor of 3-4, while the $\nue$ rates are enhanced by a factor of $\sim$10, compared to the rates obtained with a standard nuclear potential.
the neutrino cross-sections are much smaller than previously estimated and the $\nu_e/\bar{\nu}_ e$ ratio is much larger than previously estimated.

the $\bar{\nue}$ absorption cross-section is much lower than that of the $\nue$ absorption cross-section, and that both of these absorption cross-sections are much smaller than those calculated in a free-space environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neutrino-spectrum of a supernova is strongly affected by the nuclear equation of state.
the charged-current rates for neutrinos and anti-neutrinos are not the same.
the $\bar{\nue}$ absorption cross-section in the neutrinosphere is much smaller than previously thought.
